title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: 63% feel negative about grocery shopping – up 13 points from a year ago
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**‘TRIGGERED’ IN THE GROCERY AISLE**


Americans are increasingly “triggered” in the grocery aisle, as affordability pressures and distrust of large companies shape how they shop and eat, based on[Harris Poll](https://lnkd.in/p/g-uEweMd) research.


- 77% of U.S. adults cite cost of living are the most significant source of stress in their lives.
- 51% of Americans struggle to afford groceries, with consumers spending an average of 11.2% of their income on them.
- 63% feel a negative emotion about grocery shopping today – up 13 points from a year ago.
- More than half of consumers say large national companies do not understand their communities’ daily lives, boosting trust in local producers and farmers markets.
- Younger consumers increasingly favor home-cooked dinners and backyard barbecues to cut costs.
- 49% of Gen Z say they are “pickled obsessed” – considering it a food group for every meal.
- Parents report fewer picky eaters among their children, with 66% saying children typically devour berries before the containers make it into the refrigerator.
- *See the full deck of data at this[link](https://allisonpr.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/ap-operations/IQDNvbiPiXddQIJCyphSH3JEAezEmlKW96qCThkoNXnCKVE?e=sIIfLE)*


**THAT DATING-APP PERSON REAL OR AI?**


Single people say they’re fed up with AI-generated “catfishing,” according to new Harris Poll research with[World](https://world.org/blog/announcements/usdatingsurvey) .


- 57% say fake profiles are the biggest problem on dating apps today.
- 74% of online daters have suspected someone they matched on a dating app was not real.
- 70% would rather match with an average-looking person they know is real than a very attractive profile they can’t be sure about.
- 81% of singles would be much more likely to use a dating app if every profile was confirmed as belonging to a real person.
- 46% would be more likely to meet IRL sooner if they knew their match was a real person.


**HIGH DEMAND FOR BACK-UP CHILD CARE**


Employers’ emergency childcare offerings fall 30 points short of parents’ demands, according to the[2026 KinderCare Confidence Index, conducted with The Harris Poll.](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261029537862/en/KinderCare-Study-30-Point-Gap-Between-Parents-Child-Care-Needs-and-Employer-Support)


- 68% of parents want on-demand or emergency childcare, yet only 38% say their employers offer it.
- 81% of parents are constantly thinking about potential childcare disruptions, and more than a quarter of working parents have no backup or emergency care option.
- More than half (58%) want employer-subsidized childcare, yet only 25% say the benefit is available.
- One in two working parents have missed work due to childcare challenges, while 35% have reduced their hours.
- Two-thirds of parents say unreliable childcare negatively has affected their work performance.


**SPEED IS THE NEED FOR PACKAGE DELIVERY**


Consumers want packages at their front doors faster than ever, and this reality will continue disrupting supply chains, based on Harris Poll research with[Prologis](https://prologis.getbynder.com/asset/f50fd8ce-683e-4d32-8796-f567f99aa49a/Prologis-Consolidated-Supply-Chain-Outlook-2027.pdf) .


- The share of organizations offering same-day or next-day delivery has more than doubled, rising to 58% today from 24% in 2019.
- 91% of business leaders say customers increasingly expect delivery within a day or two.
- AI-driven demand forecasting (43%) and agentic AI systems (39%) rank among the most transformative technologies expected to reshape supply chains during the next three years.
